sections.h2: How does selling a house in Bethlehem Township work?
sections.html:
A sale in Bethlehem Township goes through an agreement of sale, a township resale inspection that produces a certificate of use and occupancy, settlement and a recorded deed. The township sits entirely in Northampton County, so the county recorder of deeds and assessment office are the same for every parcel. The township office at 4225 Easton Avenue handles the resale paperwork through its Community Development Department.

Do not confuse the township with the neighboring City of Bethlehem. The two have separate governments and separate sale rules, and this page covers only the township.

Bethlehem Township is a suburban municipality of 14.43 square miles of land northeast of the City of Bethlehem, home to an estimated 26,769 people in July 2025. The Lehigh River separates it from Lower Saucon Township to the south, and it borders Palmer, Hanover and Lower Nazareth townships along with Easton, Freemansburg and the city.

Its villages include Brodhead, Butztown, Farmersville, Middletown, Prospect Park and Wagnerville. The township was formed in 1746 as part of Bucks County and took its name from the Moravian settlement founded on Christmas Eve 1741. Students in grades nine to twelve attend Freedom High School inside the township as part of the Bethlehem Area School District, and Northampton Community College has its campus here. The climate is humid continental, with Farmersville averaging 28.8 degrees in January and 73.8 in July, so roofs, gutters and heating systems see real seasonal wear.

sections.h2: Which roads and commutes matter to buyers here?
sections.html:
Buyers in the township reach the rest of the Lehigh Valley mainly by US 22, PA 33 and PA 191. US 22 crosses the northern part along the Lehigh Valley Thruway, PA 33 runs north and south through the eastern part, and PA 191 begins at US 22 and heads north along Nazareth Pike.

  • Other major roads: William Penn Highway, Freemansburg Road, Butztown and Hecktown Roads, Farmersville Road and the Main Street Extension.
  • Road mileage: 140.29 miles of public roads in 2021, of which 113.09 miles belong to the township and 27.20 miles to PennDOT.
  • Average commute for workers: 26.1 minutes, per the Census Bureau.

sections.h2: What is the township resale inspection?
sections.html:
It is a Certificate of Use and Occupancy inspection that the Code Enforcement Officer performs for the resale of residential property and whenever a rental changes tenants. The application lives in the township's Forms and Documents list under the Property Resale/Lease Inspection Program.

  • The form asks for the premises address, the reason (residential resale or change of tenant) and the type of building, such as single-family dwelling, townhouse or condo.
  • It records the settlement date and whether the agreement of sale is attached.
  • It names a contact for scheduling: seller, buyer, or the agent or attorney.
  • The owner signs permission for the inspection.

The township says the inspection checks general compliance with its property maintenance, building and zoning rules under Ordinance Nos. 6-78 and 06-23. It is not a home inspection, the electrical portion looks only at GFCI protection, and the certificate carries no township liability for the condition of the house. Call the Code Enforcement Officer at (610) 814-6467 with questions.

sections.h2: What if the Bethlehem Township house is vacant or in foreclosure?
sections.html:
The township requires vacant properties and properties in foreclosure to be registered, and it administers the program through Hera Property Registry. Owners, mortgagees and trustees register online and pay a registration fee.

The program exists because neglected, unsecured houses draw complaints and sometimes crime, and out-of-state owners are hard to notify of violations. If you inherited an empty house or fell behind on a mortgage, register it first and then deal with the resale inspection. Most code enforcement actions start with a concern raised by a resident or owner, and the township does not accept anonymous complaints.

sections.h2: What permits and taxes affect a Bethlehem Township sale?
sections.html:
Open permits are the usual snag. After a complete building permit application, the township has fifteen business days to respond, and the work needs a Certificate of Occupancy or Compliance after final inspections. If past work was done without a permit, ask the Community Development Department how to close it out before you list.

Pennsylvania charges a 1 percent realty transfer tax on the value transferred, with seller and buyer jointly liable, and the county recorder of deeds collects it along with any local share. Ask the Northampton County Recorder of Deeds for the combined rate on your deed. For assessment appeals and the annual filing date, contact the Northampton County Assessment Division, since that office sets the deadline.

faqs.q: Do I need a township inspection to sell in Bethlehem Township?
faqs.a: Yes. The Code Enforcement Officer performs required inspections for the resale of residential property, and the buyer receives a Certificate of Use and Occupancy. Submit the Property Resale/Lease Inspection application once you have an agreement of sale and a settlement date.

faqs.q: Is the Bethlehem Township inspection the same as a home inspection?
faqs.a: No. The township form says its purpose is general compliance with property maintenance, building and zoning rules. Electrical review covers only GFCI items, and the township takes no responsibility for the home's condition.

faqs.q: Does the City of Bethlehem sale inspection apply to my township house?
faqs.a: No. The city's rule covers property inside city limits. A house in Bethlehem Township uses the township's resale program, even though the mailing address says Bethlehem.

faqs.q: Which county records a Bethlehem Township deed?
faqs.a: Northampton County. The Recorder of Deeds there records the deed and collects the Pennsylvania transfer tax with any local share.

faqs.q: What if my Bethlehem Township house is vacant?
faqs.a: Register it. The township runs a vacant and foreclosure property registry through Hera Property Registry, and owners, mortgagees and trustees must register online and pay the fee.
